replies.text: {"what_it_does":"No owner intent recorded; this is read from the list. It is a Temur (U/R/G) legendary-artifact and equipment deck. Lara Croft, Tomb Raider attacks to exile a legendary artifact or land from a graveyard and play it, and her raid trigger makes a token (the table text is cut off). Graveyard fillers like Goblin Engineer, Emry, Lurker of the Loch, Faithless Looting and Thirst for Knowledge feed her, and Treasure doublers (Academy Manufactor, Xorn, Jolene, the Plunder Queen) plus 17 ramp pieces fund it. Equipment such as Embercleave, Lost Jitte and the two Andúrils is the damage payload.","central_concept":{"summary":"Lara Croft attacks every turn to replay legendary artifacts and lands from graveyards, and legendary equipment turns those attacks into damage and card advantage.","key_cards":["Lara Croft, Tomb Raider","Goblin Engineer","Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Academy Ruins","Reckless Handling","Thirst for Knowledge","Swiftfoot Boots","Mithril Coat"]},"win_paths":[{"path":"Infinite combat and Treasure loop: The Reaver Cleaver with Aggravated Assault (untap creatures, extra combat, and Treasure from combat damage); the facts list this as a complete combo producing infinite mana and infinite combat phases","basis":"inferred_from_list","key_cards":["The Reaver Cleaver","Aggravated Assault","Xorn","Academy Manufactor"]},{"path":"Equipped legendary attackers: Lara or another legendary creature carries equipment through combat. Embercleave gives double strike and trample, Andúril, Flame of the West makes attacking Spirit tokens, and Blackblade Reforged and Andúril, Narsil Reforged scale the damage","basis":"inferred_from_list","key_cards":["Embercleave","Andúril, Flame of the West","Andúril, Narsil Reforged","Blackblade Reforged","Lost Jitte","Shadowspear"]},{"path":"The Millennium Calendar doubling to 1,000 time counters for a 1,000 life loss, as a slow alternate win","basis":"inferred_from_list","key_cards":["The Millennium Calendar"]}],"success_criteria":["Lara has a legal exile target (a legendary artifact or land in a graveyard) on most attack turns. Check that enough self-mill, discard and tutor-to-graveyard effects exist: Goblin Engineer, Emry, Lurker of the Loch, Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Thirst for Knowledge, Reckless Handling, Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift.","Lara survives to attack and connects. Check the protection suite: Swiftfoot Boots, Mithril Coat, Hammer of Nazahn, Heroic Intervention, K-9, Mark I and Winged Boots.","Five or more mana is reachable by turn 4 or 5 so Aggravated Assault is castable and activatable. This rests on 17 ramp pieces, the Treasure doublers and a 2.75 average mana value.","The two combo pieces, The Reaver Cleaver and Aggravated Assault, can be assembled with tutors (Fabricate, Reckless Handling, Goblin Engineer) and protected from counterspells (Chimil, the Inner Sun, Delighted Halfling).","Card flow stays steady: 14 draw effects plus Jhoira, Weatherlight Captain, The Reality Chip and The Key to the Vault keep the equipment and graveyard engine supplied.","Interaction is available while developing: 6 targeted removal and 2 wipes. Anger of the Gods and Blasphemous Act should be checked for how well they coexist with an indestructible-equipment board."],"intentional_quirks":[{"quirk":"Many legendary lands and legendary artifacts that matter only because of Lara's attack trigger and the legendary-creature lands","cards":["Academy Ruins","Rivendell","The Shire","The Grey Havens","Otawara, Soaring City","Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth","Lost Jitte","Shadowspear"],"why_deliberate":"Lara's trigger targets only legendary artifact or land cards. Rivendell and The Shire care about controlling a legendary creature, and The Grey Havens and Otawara, Soaring City reward legendary matters."},{"quirk":"Equipment-heavy list with only 16 creatures to carry it","cards":["Embercleave","Lost Jitte","Shadowspear","Blackblade Reforged","The Reaver Cleaver","Sword of the Animist","Tarrian's Soulcleaver","Hammer of Nazahn"],"why_deliberate":"The profile lists equipment as a strong archetype affinity (0.80). Many pieces are legendary and so feed Lara's graveyard-replay trigger, and Hammer of Nazahn and The Reality Chip add attach-on-entry and reconfigure value."},{"quirk":"The Millennium Calendar as a slow, unusual alternate win condition","cards":["The Millennium Calendar"],"why_deliberate":"The profile says the owner enjoys wacky concepts. It is a legendary artifact, so it fits Lara's trigger, and the list has untap effects (Aggravated Assault) to support it."}],"power_target":{"stated":false,"bracket":null,"note":"No bracket is recorded in the intent or profile. The computed minimum is bracket 3, from the Game Changer The One Ring and the two-card combo The Reaver Cleaver + Aggravated Assault. That is a floor, not the owner's target."},"questions_for_owner":[{"question":"What bracket or power level should this deck land at?","why_asked":"The facts put the floor at bracket 3 (The One Ring plus an infinite combo). If you want 3, reviewers should treat the combo as a ceiling and judge tutors and fast mana accordingly. If you want 4 or higher, they should push consistency and protection. If you want lower, The One Ring and the combo would be flagged."},{"question":"Is the Aggravated Assault and The Reaver Cleaver infinite loop an intended win, or an accidental interaction you would avoid or cut?","why_asked":"If it is intended, the review should measure how reliably the deck assembles and protects it. If it is accidental, the review should treat it as a power-level risk and consider cuts, and would weight the equipment-combat and Millennium Calendar paths more heavily."},{"question":"Is Passionate Archaeologist meant to be a second commander alongside Lara Croft, or is it an intended card in the 99?","why_asked":"The list totals 100 cards with only Lara as commander, so the Background sits in the 99, where it normally does nothing. If it is a pet or placeholder, the review will not flag it. If it should be a second commander, the card count and the exile-cast burn plan (Faldorn, Dread Wolf Herald, Chimil, the Inner Sun, Urza, Lord High Artificer) change."},{"question":"Is the Lara Croft graveyard-exile and legendary theme mandatory, or just flavor around a general artifact, Treasure and equipment deck?","why_asked":"If the theme is mandatory, non-legendary artifacts and self-mill density should be judged by how well they feed Lara. If it is flavor, the review can trade them for stronger artifact and Treasure pieces."},{"question":"Do you have a budget cap or a list of cards that must stay?","why_asked":"The list is about $612, with expensive cards such as The One Ring ($107.84), Shadowspear and Aggravated Assault. A cap would change which swaps can be suggested. Must-keeps would be treated as quirks and not criticized."}]}

replies.label: B:plan_synergy
replies.text: {"axis_score":{"score":8,"one_line":"Goblin Engineer, Emry, the looting suite and Otawara's channel reliably stock the graveyard with legendary artifacts and lands for Lara. The engine is tight, and its few leaks are small: a Background in the 99, two symmetrical wipes, and Treasure handed to opponents."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"Lara's attack trigger has dedicated enablers that put its exact target type into the graveyard. Goblin Engineer tutors a legendary equipment like The Reaver Cleaver or Embercleave straight into the yard. Thirst for Knowledge, Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Big Score and Reckless Handling discard artifacts. Otawara, Soaring City channels itself into the yard as a legendary land. Lara then exiles and replays these, so a 'discard' becomes card advantage instead of a cost.","evidence":{"cards":["Lara Croft, Tomb Raider","Goblin Engineer","The Reaver Cleaver","Embercleave","Thirst for Knowledge","Faithless Looting","Frantic Search","Reckless Handling","Otawara, Soaring City"],"fact_keys":["deck.commanders"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.8,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"The graveyard-replay plan does not collapse if Lara is removed. Emry, Lurker of the Loch casts artifacts from the graveyard, and Goblin Engineer's activation returns cheap artifacts. Daretti, Scrap Savant's -2 and Academy Ruins also recur artifacts, so the same yard Lara feeds on stays live without her. The synergy.orphans list wrongly includes Emry and most equipment; its tag heuristic misses this whole engine.","evidence":{"cards":["Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Goblin Engineer","Daretti, Scrap Savant","Academy Ruins"],"fact_keys":["roles.recursion.cards","synergy.orphans","synergy.orphan_definition"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"Treasure is a real second engine. Xorn, Jolene, the Plunder Queen and Academy Manufactor multiply Treasure from The Reaver Cleaver, Storm the Vault, Big Score and Rashmi and Ragavan. That surplus pays the expensive equip costs on Embercleave, Andúril, Narsil Reforged and Blackblade Reforged. Hammer of Nazahn's free attach further reduces the equip tax. Lara's raid token text is truncated in the table, so its contribution is unverified.","evidence":{"cards":["Xorn","Jolene, the Plunder Queen","Academy Manufactor","The Reaver Cleaver","Storm the Vault // Vault of Catlacan","Hammer of Nazahn","Andúril, Narsil Reforged"],"fact_keys":["roles.ramp.count","roles.ramp_vs_norm.target"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.7,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"Passionate Archaeologist is a Background sitting in the 99 with Lara as the sole commander. Its text only grants abilities to commander creatures, so as a card in the deck it does nothing. It is the one true island in an otherwise connected list. Whether it is a mistake hinges on q-3.","evidence":{"cards":["Passionate Archaeologist","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider"],"fact_keys":["deck.card_count","deck.commanders"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.5,"depends_on_questions":["q-3"],"fix_direction":"Either declare it as a second commander and trim the 99 by one, or replace it with another enabler that puts legendary artifacts or lands into the graveyard."},{"claim":"Both wipes are symmetrical against a deck with few equipment carriers (derived.type_counts.creature). Blasphemous Act kills Lara, Jolene, Xorn and Academy Manufactor along with opponents' boards. Anger of the Gods exiles the small utility bodies (Delighted Halfling, Etherium Sculptor, Goblin Engineer), so the equipment is left with no one to carry it. Only Mithril Coat, Hammer of Nazahn and Heroic Intervention save part of the board.","evidence":{"cards":["Blasphemous Act","Anger of the Gods","Mithril Coat","Hammer of Nazahn","Heroic Intervention"],"fact_keys":["roles.wipes.cards","derived.type_counts.creature"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.6,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"Swap one wipe for a one-sided or noncreature-focused sweeper, or for bounce that leaves your equipment carriers standing."},{"claim":"The Millennium Calendar only gains counters during your untap step, so Aggravated Assault's mid-turn untap adds nothing to it, contrary to the brief's rationale. The Calendar is a chosen quirk. Its real cost is that it relies solely on its own {2},{T} doubling and has no in-deck accelerant.","evidence":{"cards":["The Millennium Calendar","Aggravated Assault"],"fact_keys":[]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.8,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"If the Calendar win should be real, add a way to untap the Calendar itself or proliferate counters. Otherwise, accept it as a flavor inclusion."},{"claim":"Two cards hand opponents Treasure. Jolene, the Plunder Queen gives a Treasure to any player who attacks your opponents. An Offer You Can't Refuse gives its target two Treasures. In a deck whose engine is Treasure, these feed rivals' mana too.","evidence":{"cards":["Jolene, the Plunder Queen","An Offer You Can't Refuse"],"fact_keys":["roles.targeted_removal.cards"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.55,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"Consider a cheap counter without the symmetrical gift. Keep Jolene only if her doubling outweighs the shared Treasure at your table."}]}

replies.label: B:budget_inventory
replies.text: {"axis_score":{"score":8,"one_line":"No cap is set (derived.price.over_hard_cap UNAVAILABLE), and nearly every pricey card serves Lara's legendary plan; the only debatable spend is The One Ring at $107.84, which hinges on q-1 and q-5."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"Most of the top spend buys parts of the brief's central plan. Mithril Coat ($24.43) and Delighted Halfling ($24.16) protect Lara and resolve legendary spells. The Reaver Cleaver ($28.90) is the Treasure payload. Shadowspear ($34.91) gives trample and lifelink, and as a legendary artifact it is a Lara replay target.","evidence":{"cards":["Mithril Coat","Delighted Halfling","The Reaver Cleaver","Shadowspear"],"fact_keys":["derived.price.most_expensive.Mithril Coat.usd","derived.price.most_expensive.Delighted Halfling.usd","derived.price.most_expensive.The Reaver Cleaver.usd","derived.price.most_expensive.Shadowspear.usd"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"The graveyard engine that makes Lara work is very cheap. Emry, Lurker of the Loch ($0.65), Reckless Handling ($0.36), Faithless Looting ($0.76) and Goblin Engineer ($8.88) carry the success criterion of always having an exile target. The deck's identity is therefore not price-locked.","evidence":{"cards":["Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Reckless Handling","Faithless Looting","Goblin Engineer"],"fact_keys":[]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.8,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"The One Ring is the single largest spend ($107.84) and the deck's only Game Changer. Its role is generic card draw and one turn of protection rather than anything specific to Lara, though it is a legendary artifact she can replay. Whether that money is well spent depends on the owner's bracket target and budget, both still open.","evidence":{"cards":["The One Ring"],"fact_keys":["derived.price.most_expensive.The One Ring.usd","bracket.game_changers","derived.price.total_usd"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.4,"depends_on_questions":["q-1","q-5"],"fix_direction":"If the owner wants a lower bracket or a cheaper list, swap it for a cheaper legendary artifact that draws cards. That keeps Lara's replay targets, at the cost of a weaker card-advantage burst."},{"claim":"Aggravated Assault ($37.17) is the deck's third-priciest card, and its value rests almost entirely on the infinite loop with The Reaver Cleaver. If that combo is not intended, the $37.17 buys only a single extra combat per activation.","evidence":{"cards":["Aggravated Assault","The Reaver Cleaver"],"fact_keys":["derived.price.most_expensive.Aggravated Assault.usd"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.4,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":"If the combo is unwanted, use a cheaper extra-combat or untap effect that does not go infinite with Treasure-on-damage."},{"claim":"The $611.9 total is a floor, not the real cost. Seventeen entries are unpriced, including the shocklands Breeding Pool, Steam Vents and Stomping Ground, plus Academy Ruins and Sol Ring. Ownership also cannot be judged, because inventory data is unavailable.","evidence":{"cards":["Breeding Pool","Steam Vents","Stomping Ground","Academy Ruins"],"fact_keys":["derived.price.unpriced_cards","derived.price.total_usd","derived.inventory"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.9,"depends_on_questions":["q-5"],"fix_direction":"Supply prices for the unpriced cards and an owned-card inventory so the true cost of completing the list can be stated."}]}

replies.label: B:power_bracket
replies.text: {"axis_score":{"score":7,"one_line":"The floor is bracket 3 (bracket.minimum_bracket), set only by The One Ring and the Aggravated Assault + Reaver Cleaver combo; the owner's target is unstated (q-1), so fit cannot be fully judged."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"The bracket floor is cleanly bounded. Only one Game Changer (The One Ring) and one two-card combo (Aggravated Assault + The Reaver Cleaver) set bracket 3, and Lara's salt is very low. If the owner wants to move brackets, that is a two- or three-card decision, not a rebuild.","evidence":{"cards":["The One Ring","Aggravated Assault","The Reaver Cleaver"],"fact_keys":["bracket.minimum_bracket","bracket.reasons.game_changers.cards","bracket.reasons.two_card_combos.cards","edhrec.commander.salt"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.9,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"The Reaver Cleaver half of the combo is easy to reach on-theme. Fabricate and Reckless Handling tutor it, and Goblin Engineer can bin it so Lara's attack trigger exiles it with a discovery counter and replays it. The combo grows out of the commander's engine rather than sitting bolted on.","evidence":{"cards":["The Reaver Cleaver","Goblin Engineer","Fabricate","Reckless Handling","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider"],"fact_keys":["roles.tutors.cards","combos.complete.3750-5039.card_names"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"The combo is lopsided for a higher-bracket target. All three tutors (Fabricate, Reckless Handling, Goblin Engineer) find only artifacts, so Aggravated Assault, an enchantment, can only be drawn or hit off Chimil, the Inner Sun's discover. Fast mana (Sol Ring, Delighted Halfling) and ramp well above the 9-11 target speed the deck up, but the win stays draw-dependent, which reads as a mid bracket 3. This only matters if the owner wants bracket 4 (q-1) and treats the loop as an intended win (q-2).","evidence":{"cards":["Aggravated Assault","Fabricate","Reckless Handling","Goblin Engineer","Chimil, the Inner Sun","Sol Ring","Delighted Halfling"],"fact_keys":["roles.tutors.count","roles.tutors.cards","roles.ramp.count","roles.ramp.target_max"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.45,"depends_on_questions":["q-1","q-2"],"fix_direction":"If pushing to bracket 4 with the combo as the plan, add a way to find or recur enchantments, or a second untap/extra-combat enabler that pairs with the Cleaver; if staying at 3, leave it as a ceiling."},{"claim":"If the owner wants bracket 2 or a casual table, The One Ring and the Aggravated Assault + The Reaver Cleaver loop both break the bracket rules. The One Ring is also the single most expensive card, which ties into the budget question.","evidence":{"cards":["The One Ring","Aggravated Assault","The Reaver Cleaver"],"fact_keys":["bracket.game_changers","bracket.reasons.two_card_combos.floor","derived.price.most_expensive.The One Ring.usd"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.4,"depends_on_questions":["q-1","q-2","q-5"],"fix_direction":"For a lower target, replace the Game Changer with a non-Game-Changer card-draw artifact, and replace one combo half with a non-infinite extra-combat or Treasure-on-damage piece."}]}

replies.label: B:win_paths_closing
replies.text: {"axis_score":{"score":7,"one_line":"A real two-card kill exists (combos.complete.3750-5039), and The Reaver Cleaver half is very findable, but Aggravated Assault is a lone, untutorable enchantment and the fair paths close slowly."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"The Reaver Cleaver half of the infinite is unusually easy to reach. Fabricate and Reckless Handling tutor it to hand. Goblin Engineer tutors it into the graveyard, where Lara Croft's attack trigger can exile and play it (it is a legendary artifact), or Emry, Lurker of the Loch can cast it. Goblin Engineer and Daretti, Scrap Savant can also rebuild it after removal.","evidence":{"cards":["The Reaver Cleaver","Goblin Engineer","Fabricate","Reckless Handling","Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider","Daretti, Scrap Savant"],"fact_keys":["roles.tutors.cards","roles.recursion.cards","combos.complete.3750-5039.card_names"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"Treasure doublers lower the combo's threshold. Aggravated Assault costs five mana per extra combat. With Xorn or Jolene, the Plunder Queen (Jolene also makes a Treasure on each attack), a Cleaver carrier needs to deal only about 3-4 damage to pay for the next combat. Embercleave's double strike makes Cleaver trigger twice per combat. So even Lara Croft, Tomb Raider with modest equipment can go infinite.","evidence":{"cards":["Xorn","Jolene, the Plunder Queen","Academy Manufactor","Embercleave","The Reaver Cleaver","Aggravated Assault"],"fact_keys":["combos.complete.3750-5039.produces"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.65,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"Aggravated Assault is the deck's single point of failure. All three tutors (Fabricate, Reckless Handling, Goblin Engineer) find only artifacts, and both recursion pieces return only artifacts. So the enchantment half of the only complete combo is found only by natural draws, and one enchantment-removal spell ends that path for the game. This matters only if the combo is intended (q-2).","evidence":{"cards":["Aggravated Assault","Fabricate","Reckless Handling","Goblin Engineer","Daretti, Scrap Savant"],"fact_keys":["roles.tutors.cards","roles.recursion.cards","combos.complete.3750-5039.card_names"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.5,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":"Add a way to find or recur enchantments, or a second extra-combat or untap effect that also pairs with The Reaver Cleaver, so the combo is not a single untutorable card."},{"claim":"Without the infinite, the fair equipment path has no mass finisher. Embercleave, Andúril, Flame of the West, Andúril, Narsil Reforged and Blackblade Reforged each boost one or two attackers. With only 16 creatures (a deliberate quirk), damage comes in one large hit per turn that a single chump block or removal spell blunts. If q-2 says the combo goes, games will drag after the board is built.","evidence":{"cards":["Embercleave","Andúril, Flame of the West","Andúril, Narsil Reforged","Blackblade Reforged","Lost Jitte"],"fact_keys":["combos.counts.complete"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.45,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":"Add a team-wide finisher (a mass pump or evasion effect, or a token-and-anthem burst) that turns a modest board into lethal across the table in one turn."},{"claim":"The Millennium Calendar is a chosen quirk, but the brief's support for it does not hold. Aggravated Assault untaps only creatures, and the Calendar taps to double, so it doubles at most once per turn. It gains counters only from untap steps, so it needs many turns of survival to reach 1,000. Treat it as flavor, not as a closing path.","evidence":{"cards":["The Millennium Calendar","Aggravated Assault"],"fact_keys":[]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.8,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"If the Calendar is meant to be a live win, add effects that untap artifacts or permanents. Otherwise accept it as a slow pet card."}]}

replies.label: B:concept_execution
replies.text: {"axis_score":{"score":7,"one_line":"Lara has many legendary artifact and land targets and backup recursion (Academy Ruins, Emry, Goblin Engineer), but true self-mill is thin, so early attack triggers often whiff; her raid text is cut off in the table, so its value could not be judged."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"Almost every payoff the deck cares about is itself a legal Lara target. The Reaver Cleaver, Embercleave, Mithril Coat, Shadowspear, Lost Jitte, The One Ring and The Millennium Calendar are all legendary artifacts, and Academy Ruins, Otawara, Soaring City and Rivendell are legendary lands. Whatever gets milled, discarded or destroyed becomes a replay on the next attack, and combo half The Reaver Cleaver can be rebuilt from the graveyard after removal.","evidence":{"cards":["Lara Croft, Tomb Raider","The Reaver Cleaver","Embercleave","Mithril Coat","Shadowspear","The One Ring","Academy Ruins","Otawara, Soaring City"],"fact_keys":[]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.85,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"Graveyard recovery of artifacts does not rest on Lara alone. Emry, Lurker of the Loch casts artifacts from the graveyard, Goblin Engineer tutors an artifact straight into the graveyard and can reanimate cheap ones, Academy Ruins tops them, and Daretti, Scrap Savant returns them. If Lara is answered, the 'legendary artifacts come back' identity of the deck survives.","evidence":{"cards":["Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Goblin Engineer","Academy Ruins","Daretti, Scrap Savant"],"fact_keys":["roles.recursion.cards","roles.tutors.cards"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"Faldorn, Dread Wolf Herald turns each Lara replay into a 2/2 Wolf. Replays are spells cast from exile or lands entering from exile, and Rose, Cutthroat Raider's Junk and Urza, Lord High Artificer's exile-play stack more of these triggers. The concept generates board presence, not just card recovery.","evidence":{"cards":["Faldorn, Dread Wolf Herald","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider","Rose, Cutthroat Raider","Urza, Lord High Artificer"],"fact_keys":[]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.7,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"Most graveyard fillers are loot or discard effects: Faithless Looting, Frantic Search, Thirst for Knowledge, Big Score, Windfall and Reckless Handling (random discard). These only bin a legendary if one is already in hand, so you trade a card you could just cast. Real top-of-library filling is limited to Emry's mill 4, The Everflowing Well's mill 2 and Search for Azcanta's surveil. Unless Goblin Engineer is drawn, or an opponent's graveyard happens to hold a legendary, Lara's turn 4-5 attacks often have no target.","evidence":{"cards":["Faithless Looting","Frantic Search","Thirst for Knowledge","Reckless Handling","Emry, Lurker of the Loch","The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools","Search for Azcanta // Azcanta, the Sunken Ruin","Goblin Engineer"],"fact_keys":["roles.draw.cards"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.6,"depends_on_questions":["q-4"],"fix_direction":"Add one or two cheap self-mill or entomb-style effects that put artifacts or lands straight from the library into the graveyard, cut from the generic land-fetch ramp, which is above the norm (roles.ramp_vs_norm.count)."},{"claim":"The computed artifacts cluster is not commander-centered, and much of the equipment payload shows up as orphans: The Key to the Vault, Lost Jitte, Andúril, Flame of the West and Winged Boots. The list reads as 'artifact pile plus Lara' more than 'Lara engine'. The orphan flag partly reflects clustering limits, since these are legendary and do feed her, so treat it as a soft signal.","evidence":{"cards":["The Key to the Vault","Winged Boots","Andúril, Flame of the West"],"fact_keys":["synergy.clusters.artifacts.commander_centered","synergy.orphans","synergy.density"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.4,"depends_on_questions":["q-4"],"fix_direction":"Favor support cards that reward playing from exile or the graveyard over generic artifact-count cards."},{"claim":"Passionate Archaeologist is the strongest possible payoff for Lara's exile-play: it deals burn equal to the mana value of each spell cast from exile. But it is a Background sitting in the 99, where it does nothing. Whether this is a gap hinges on q-3.","evidence":{"cards":["Passionate Archaeologist"],"fact_keys":["deck.card_count","deck.commanders"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.45,"depends_on_questions":["q-3"],"fix_direction":"Either make it a second commander and cut a card from the 99, or replace it with a card that pays off casting spells from exile from within the 99."}]}

replies.label: B:interaction_resilience
replies.text: {"axis_score":{"score":6,"one_line":"Layered protection and artifact recursion keep the engine alive, but only Beast Within and Chaos Warp answer arbitrary creatures or enchantments (roles.targeted_removal.count 6 vs target_min 11)."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"Lara is protected in layers. Swiftfoot Boots and Winged Boots stop targeted removal, Mithril Coat (flash, auto-attaches to a legendary) and Hammer of Nazahn give indestructible against wipes, K-9, Mark I adds ward to other legendaries, and Heroic Intervention covers the whole board at instant speed. This directly serves the brief's 'Lara survives to attack' criterion.","evidence":{"cards":["Swiftfoot Boots","Winged Boots","Mithril Coat","Hammer of Nazahn","Heroic Intervention","K-9, Mark I"],"fact_keys":["roles.protection.count","roles.protection.cards"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.8,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"Artifact removal is undone by the deck's own engine. Goblin Engineer and Daretti, Scrap Savant return artifacts to the battlefield, Emry, Lurker of the Loch recasts them, Academy Ruins stacks them back on top, and Lara's attack trigger replays any destroyed legendary equipment. A Vandalblast-style overload costs the deck tempo, not the game.","evidence":{"cards":["Goblin Engineer","Daretti, Scrap Savant","Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Academy Ruins","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider"],"fact_keys":["roles.recursion.cards"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"The two wipes become one-sided on the right turn. Blasphemous Act or Anger of the Gods cast while Lara holds Mithril Coat or Hammer of Nazahn, or with Heroic Intervention up, clears blockers, and the equipment survives the wipe to re-equip. This answers the brief's check on whether the wipes coexist with the equipment board: they do, if sequenced.","evidence":{"cards":["Blasphemous Act","Anger of the Gods","Mithril Coat","Hammer of Nazahn","Heroic Intervention"],"fact_keys":["roles.wipes.cards"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.65,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"Creature removal is very thin for a combat deck. Of the 6 counted removal pieces, three are counterspells (Counterspell, Arcane Denial, An Offer You Can't Refuse), Vandalblast hits only artifacts, and Bow of Nylea only pings fliers for 2. That leaves Beast Within, plus the uncounted Chaos Warp and Otawara, Soaring City bounce, against a resolved creature threat or a deathtouch blocker that stops Lara connecting.","evidence":{"cards":["Beast Within","Chaos Warp","Otawara, Soaring City","Bow of Nylea","Vandalblast","Counterspell"],"fact_keys":["roles.targeted_removal.count","roles.targeted_removal.target_min","roles.targeted_removal.cards"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.75,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"Add two or three cheap instant-speed creature answers in red or blue (burn, bounce or fight-style removal that rides on Lara's first strike), ideally replacing low-impact utility slots."},{"claim":"Graveyard hate aimed at this player blunts Goblin Engineer, Emry, Lurker of the Loch, Academy Ruins and Daretti, Scrap Savant all at once. Lara can still mine opponents' graveyards, so the engine degrades rather than stops. The only ways to remove a hostile enchantment or artifact stax piece are Beast Within, Chaos Warp, Otawara, Soaring City bounce, and Vandalblast for artifacts. How much this matters depends on whether the Lara graveyard theme is mandatory.","evidence":{"cards":["Goblin Engineer","Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Academy Ruins","Beast Within","Chaos Warp","Otawara, Soaring City"],"fact_keys":["roles.recursion.cards"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.45,"depends_on_questions":["q-4"],"fix_direction":"Add a flexible artifact/enchantment answer (a green naturalize-style effect, ideally on a creature or instant) to clear graveyard-hate and stax permanents."},{"claim":"If the Aggravated Assault + The Reaver Cleaver loop is the intended finish, the combo has little protection. Aggravated Assault is an enchantment that only Heroic Intervention protects, and anti-counter coverage rests on Delighted Halfling (legendary spells only, so not Aggravated Assault) and a 6-mana Chimil, the Inner Sun. With only three counterspells, the deck struggles to force the loop through opposing interaction.","evidence":{"cards":["Aggravated Assault","The Reaver Cleaver","Heroic Intervention","Delighted Halfling","Chimil, the Inner Sun","Counterspell","Arcane Denial"],"fact_keys":[]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.45,"depends_on_questions":["q-2","q-1"],"fix_direction":"If the combo is intended, add a cheap free or one-mana protective counter, or another hexproof/indestructible effect for noncreature permanents; if not, this finding drops."},{"claim":"Wipes sit at 2 against a 5 norm, and Blasphemous Act kills the deck's other 15 creatures, including the Treasure doublers Xorn and Academy Manufactor. Against a go-wide table, the deck has few ways to reset the board without also resetting its own mana engine.","evidence":{"cards":["Blasphemous Act","Anger of the Gods","Xorn","Academy Manufactor"],"fact_keys":["roles.wipes.count","roles.wipes.target_min"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.55,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"Consider one more mass-removal effect that is one-sided or scales (damage-based on attackers, or bounce), rather than another symmetrical wipe."}]}

replies.text:
{"axis_score":{"score":7,"one_line":"17 ramp pieces (roles.ramp.count) on a 2.75 curve carry 35 lands well. The red and blue land counts, 16 each against 28 and 30 recommended, leave the double-pip cards and Aggravated Assault leaning on rocks and Treasure."},"no_significant_problems":false,"strengths":[{"claim":"The cheap ramp suite makes the commander and the 5-mana Aggravated Assault activation reachable on time. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Delighted Halfling, Farseek and Nature's Lore sit in the 1-2 slots, and there are 19 two-drops and 21 three-drops with almost nothing above 4. Lara can land on turn 2-3 and attack with mana to spare. Farseek and Nature's Lore can fetch Breeding Pool, Steam Vents and Stomping Ground by land type, so the ramp also fixes colors.","evidence":{"cards":["Sol Ring","Arcane Signet","Delighted Halfling","Farseek","Nature's Lore","Breeding Pool","Steam Vents","Stomping Ground","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider"],"fact_keys":["roles.ramp.count","curve.average_mv","curve.buckets.2.count","curve.buckets.3.count","curve.buckets.5.count"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.8,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""},{"claim":"Lara's attack trigger has dependable fuel. Goblin Engineer puts a legendary artifact straight into the graveyard on entry, Emry, Lurker of the Loch mills four, and Thirst for Knowledge discards an artifact as its natural cost. Otawara, Soaring City puts itself in the graveyard via channel. Lara will usually have a legal exile target from turn 3-4 rather than attacking with an empty trigger.","evidence":{"cards":["Goblin Engineer","Emry, Lurker of the Loch","Thirst for Knowledge","Otawara, Soaring City","Faithless Looting","Lara Croft, Tomb Raider"],"fact_keys":["roles.tutors.cards","roles.draw.count"]},"severity":"high","confidence":0.7,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":""}],"problems":[{"claim":"Red and blue land sources fall well short of what the double-pip cards want.
- Red: 16 sources against 28 recommended, with 24 pips. Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R} activation and Faithless Looting's flashback both need red.
- Blue: 16 sources against 30 recommended. Counterspell needs UU, and Academy Ruins, K-9, Mark I, Rivendell and The Reality Chip all need {U} activations.
- Colorless lands dilute both further: Academy Ruins, Reliquary Tower, Temple of the False God and The Grey Havens (colorless unless a legendary creature is in the graveyard).
- Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth only adds green, which is already the lightest color (11 pips).
- Arcane Signet and Treasure from Xorn, Jolene, the Plunder Queen and Big Score patch the gap. Sol Ring and Thought Vessel cannot.","evidence":{"cards":["Aggravated Assault","Counterspell","Academy Ruins","Reliquary Tower","Temple of the False God","The Grey Havens","Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth","Sol Ring","Thought Vessel"],"fact_keys":["mana.pips_vs_sources.R.sources","mana.pips_vs_sources.R.recommended_sources","mana.pips_vs_sources.U.sources","mana.pips_vs_sources.U.recommended_sources","mana.pips_vs_sources.G.pips","mana.norms.colored_sources.caveat"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.65,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"Trade one or two colorless utility lands for untapped blue-red or red-producing duals. Alternatively, swap a colorless rock for a color-producing one."},{"claim":"The three tutors are all artifact-only, so they can find The Reaver Cleaver but never Aggravated Assault, an enchantment. The tutors are Fabricate, Reckless Handling and Goblin Engineer. The brief's goal of assembling the combo with tutors is therefore only half met: Assault must be drawn naturally. This matters only if the combo is an intended win (q-2). If it is not, this is irrelevant.","evidence":{"cards":["Aggravated Assault","The Reaver Cleaver","Fabricate","Reckless Handling","Goblin Engineer"],"fact_keys":["roles.tutors.count","roles.tutors.cards"]},"severity":"med","confidence":0.45,"depends_on_questions":["q-2"],"fix_direction":"If the combo is intended, add a way to find or recur enchantments, or more card selection to dig for it."},{"claim":"The mana.mdfc_spell_lands count of 5 overstates the land count. The five cards are transforming spells, not modal double-faced cards, and none can be played as a land drop: Search for Azcanta, Storm the Vault, The Everflowing Well, Matzalantli and Brass's Tunnel-Grinder. Each needs a graveyard, artifact or descend threshold before it becomes a land. The true land count is 35 against the 38 norm. The 17 ramp pieces largely cover that, but early land-light hands are slightly riskier than the facts suggest.","evidence":{"cards":["Search for Azcanta // Azcanta, the Sunken Ruin","Storm the Vault // Vault of Catlacan","The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools","Matzalantli, the Great Door // The Core","Brass's Tunnel-Grinder // Tecutlan, the Searing Rift"],"fact_keys":["mana.mdfc_spell_lands","mana.lands","mana.norms.lands.target"]},"severity":"low","confidence":0.7,"depends_on_questions":[],"fix_direction":"No change needed if the ramp density stays; mulligan hands as though there are 35 lands, not 40."}]}
